# OUTLINE — *The Long Book*

120,000 words · 46 chapters · ~2,600 words each · dual third limited past,
alternating (Sahra odd, Yannu even, with a deliberate break at ch 44–45).

Beat vocabulary: Save the Cat carrying the plot spine, Romancing the Beat
carrying the relationship's four phases, one label set.

The book runs from 9 Thaw 1219 to 27 Deepwinter 1219 — ten months, ending on
the year's lowest tides.

---

# PART 1 — CHAPTERS

## ACT I (ch 1–11, 0–24%)

**ch 1 — 2% — Sahra — Third Reach, low water — 9 Thaw**
*Plot: Opening Image / Setup · Romance: Setup*

Sahra clears two bays of rot from the Ferrey granary alone at dawn, naming
the load aloud to an empty floor because she has been reading herself into a
book since she was nine. Establish: the sweetness at the wrists, the give in
the knees, nine of fourteen, the chipped cup that does nothing. Weyl Ammar,
the fen's hired setter, is four hours late and arrives with a span of grey
he cannot afford; Sahra asks what the set will cost him before she asks
whether he will do it. They set down at the Wallow's edge. Yeshin brings
breakfast and shows off — a spoiled apple gone clean in her hand — and Sahra
does not smile at it. Establish the arithmetic that governs her life: 1,806
outstanding, 334 in eight years, clear at sixty-two. Closing image: standing
water on the Wallow where standing water has no business being, and Sahra
does not know what she is looking at.

**ch 2 — 4% — Yannu — the Whiting, the Nine Marks — 11 Thaw**
*Plot: Setup / Theme Stated · Romance: Setup*

Yannu walks the spring survey of the eastern lobes and has to move three
cairns inward — 129 paces lost at the north lobe alone. He writes *silting*
in the warrant book and looks at the word and does not change it. Establish
grey by location, the gloves, the salt on everything, Veth's boots on the
nail. At the Kell Ammar salt-house, Yannu asks him what happens to what he
takes, and Turi holds up a grey hand: *"It isn't gone, boy. It's in me."* Then
**Turi states the theme**: *"Nothing's been paid, boy. It's only been put
somewhere."* Yannu files a false warrant
closing the north lobe. His independent goal on the page: the honest map, so
that no setter is worked to full grey for a cistern.

**ch 3 — 7% — Sahra — the Stone Ait — 20 Thaw**
*Plot: Setup · Romance: Setup*

Quarterly reckoning at the Reckoning House. Her carries entered; her balance
read aloud in a corridor full of people; an assessor reads her load off her
cuticles and enters it. The Third Order's acceleration clause is read as part
of the standard recitation and nobody remarks on it — and so is the
alienation clause, four items later in the same list, in the same voice, at
the same speed, and so is the credit rule two items after that: *a working
performed on the House's account and witnessed by a reckoner is credited to
the worker's entry at the assessed rate.* Three clauses, one breath, read
the way a clerk reads a form he has read four hundred times. Sahra is
counting her own carries against the figure the clerk just gave her and
hears none of them. **Dovra Nesuir** is
present and, citing the House's new warranting restrictions and the rate they
will cost, moves the witnessing forward from autumn 1220 to spring 1220.
Yeshin's name entered in the schedule: *capacity presumed, to be assessed at
sixteen.* Sahra signs the amendment because refusing it is a default. She
turns the tally-ring inward on the stairs.

**ch 4 — 9% — Yannu — the Low Wharfs — 24 Thaw**
*Plot: Setup · Romance: Setup*

Yannu turns down the Ammar cistern contract — four hundred carries, a
fortune — by being rude enough that they will not come back, then walks three
hours to set for a Kethren family in the Undercity for nothing while the
street floods at second tide. **Bel Osse** summons him: the House has read
six years of his warrants and wants the north lobe reopened. He refuses. She
does not argue; she notes that a hazard may be declared at any time and that
a declared hazard carries a standing order. Establish what the House can do
to him: strike the warrant, force an assessment, retire him.

**ch 5 — 11% — Sahra — Kell Ammar, the mud — 2 Green**
*Plot: **CATALYST** · Romance: **NO WAY / ADHESION*** — one event

The Wallow weeps into the Third Reach on the flood. The House declares a
hazard and issues a standing order under its warrant power: one drawer of
capacity, one warranted walker, paired, on the House's account, to survey the
lobe and stop the weep. It names Sahra Ottun, because her name is in the Long
Book and the House may compel any name in it. It names Yannu Dral.

They meet on black silt with the tide-bell going. The first working is a
shambles of mismatched rhythm: she takes faster than he can pass and nearly
seats a carry. She does the arithmetic out loud — impressment rate is one
third of open hire, which is eleven more years — and hates him on sight for
the north lobe closure that has been costing her since Rime. He does not
defend it. The one order that drags her into the Whiting's failure is the
order that pairs her with the only setter who will now be taking her carries.

**ch 6 — 13% — Yannu — the Third Reach — 5 Green**
*Plot: Debate · Romance: —*

Yannu petitions to have the order discharged; Bel Osse refuses, pleasantly.
Assessor gossip tells him what Sahra is: composed to Nesuir, a house
instrument, eleven hundred carries of somebody's collateral. He decides she
is the House's and behaves accordingly. Survey work: the weep is not surface
water. It is coming *up*. He does not put that in the warrant book yet.
Notices, against his will, that she names her loads aloud when there is
nobody on the floor.

**ch 7 — 15% — Sahra — the north lobe — 11 Green**
*Plot: Debate · Romance: **INKLING OF DESIRE***

Sahra petitions the House for release from the standing order so she can take
private hire at full rate. Refused in nine words. She and Yannu walk the north
lobe at low water; she watches him pace and refuse to round — *"It is two
hundred and eleven"* — and, at the end of the tide, she asks what the set will
cost him before she asks whether he will do it, and he stops walking. He
gives her the number: six spans this year, to the wrist on the right. The
refusal that keeps her paying at a third rate is the refusal that keeps her
beside him for the low tides, and she notices this and resents it, and the
resentment is the noticing.

**ch 8 — 17% — Yannu — the Undercity — 19 Green**
*Plot: Debate · Romance: —*

Veth's anniversary. A letter from his mother arrives nine days old and he
does not open it for two of them. He takes a set he should not — four carries
in one pass, for a fen family with a fever in the house and no rate — and it
**jumps**: he loses the smell of smoke, permanently, and finds out by not
noticing a hearth. Turi, flatly: *"That wasn't for them."* The rule of the
jump is on the page at 17%, in a chapter with no romance in it, which is where
it belongs.

**ch 9 — 20% — Sahra — the Wallow — 27 Green**
*Plot: Debate · Romance: Inkling of Desire (continuing)*

The survey grows: they must clear a mile of weeping crust to read the ground
underneath. Sahra goes to thirteen of fourteen and **the thirst goes thin** —
the first time the reader sees the edge of foundering, and Sahra's interiority
skirts the four hours at twenty-two without naming them. Yannu takes it off
her, reads her cuticles, and says the number aloud — *thirteen* — which no
assessor has ever got right. She realises he counts more honestly than the
House does, and this frightens her more than the crust did.

**ch 10 — 22% — Yannu — Nesuir house, Ferrey — 4 Highwater**
*Plot: Debate · Romance: —*

**The first of the three conversations that would end the barrier.** Sahra
goes to Dovra Nesuir and asks for release; Yannu waits in the passage with
the punt-lines and hears all of it through a door that does not shut. Dovra
says yes: bring me 2,140 carries, or a house of standing that will assume
them. Then she opens the Nesuir book, and the forward pledge, and the four
hundred tenants, and the fen tenure, and Sahra — who can read a ledger faster
than the under-reckoners — cannot fault a line of it. She leaves
understanding it better than she did going in. By 22% the reader knows the
barrier precisely, has watched it tested, and has seen the test fail on
arithmetic rather than on temper.

**ch 11 — 24% — Sahra — the Stone Ait — 12 Highwater**
*Plot: **BREAK INTO TWO** · Romance: —*

Sahra stops trying to shed the standing order and instead petitions to
**extend** it: survey the whole Wallow, not just the weep. Her reasoning is
cold and correct — if the Whiting is failing, then every carry in the Long
Book is a promise drawn on a bank with no money, and she intends to know
before Dovra does. Bel Osse grants it for her own reasons. Sahra has chosen
to walk into the Whiting, and the choice locks her into a pair with Yannu for
a season.

---

## ACT II-A (ch 12–23, 26–50%) — Fun and Games

**ch 12 — 26% — Yannu — the Low Wharfs — 20 Highwater**
*Plot: **B STORY** / Fun and Games · Romance: —*

**Sefa Quenn.** A washer with no capacity, no entry, and her
great-grandmother's arithmetic: the Whiting was a lake within family memory,
and the crust is two hundred years old, not eternal. *"Before the House, salt
was weather. Now it's owed."* Yannu takes her seriously because she counts,
and because she is the first person who has offered him a reason the ground
might have a bottom. The B Story thread — what a trade costs the people it
made obsolete, and who keeps the memory of a world before the ledger — starts
here and runs to ch 35.

**ch 13 — 28% — Sahra — Ferrey granaries — 1 Longsun**
*Plot: Fun and Games · Romance: —*

The promise of the premise: a full working, done well. Five carries, four
passes, one tide, a crowd on the bank, the granaries clean by evening. The
Draw doing exactly what the reader came for. Sahra notices the gloves — off
for the fen women, on for the Nesuir factor — and works out what he is
hiding and from whom, and it is the first hour she has liked him. The
working makes them a pair in everyone's eyes, including the factor's, who
writes it down.

**ch 14 — 30% — Yannu — Sarrow-under-Wall — 9 Longsun**
*Plot: Fun and Games · Romance: —*

**The first return.** A rot set down forty years ago comes up in the village
well. Yannu recognises his own warrant on that ground from six years back.
His falsified-warrant problem becomes a live liability in the same hour the
world plot shows its teeth. He tells Sahra half of it — the return, not the
warrants — and chooses her over the House without admitting that is what he
is doing.

**ch 15 — 33% — Sahra — Sarrow-under-Wall — 10 Longsun**
*Plot: Fun and Games · Romance: **DEEPENING DESIRE***

**The live pass** — the rule the climax will depend on, demonstrated at 33%.
The well must be cleared before the village drinks and the load is too big to
hold, so drawer and setter must work *simultaneously*, hand to hand, so that
nothing ever seats. Thirty minutes of skin against skin. He tells her flatly
that past the second knuckle he gets nothing, so if she moves she must say
so. Establish the danger: neither can stop, and whoever breaks first takes
what is in transit. The well comes clean. She keeps half a carry of rot in
her left knee for the rest of her life and does not mention it. It is the
first time either of them has touched anyone in years, and neither of them
says a word about that either.

**ch 16 — 35% — Yannu — Kell Ammar — 19 Longsun**
*Plot: Fun and Games · Romance: —*

**Halim Nesuir** comes upriver with the Nesuir factor to inspect the security.
He is kind, competent, and impossible to dislike. He and Yannu talk about
Sahra for twenty minutes without either of them saying anything. Halim gives
Yannu a pair of good gloves, unaware, because he noticed that Yannu's were
worn through, and it is the cruellest gift in the book.

**ch 17 — 37% — Sahra — Kell Ammar — 20 Longsun**
*Plot: Fun and Games · Romance: —*

**The second conversation that would end the barrier.** Sahra asks Halim to
release her. He would, in an instant, and says so, and means it — and cannot:
release is not his to give while his mother lives, and the forward pledge
stands whoever holds Nesuir, and he has four hundred tenants of his own. He
offers the only thing in his gift: he will never touch her, not once, not
ever, and nobody need know that either.

Then she asks the question the offer invites — whether she may live as she
likes — and watches him work out that he has already promised more than he
owns. He reaches the alienation clause in front of her, out loud, badly,
apologising inside the sentence: the security is the *line*, issue is
pledged from birth, and a child of hers entered outside the merger is
capacity the House has already been promised and cannot be handed. It voids
for cause. Thirty days. The fen goes, and Yeshin goes to the pump. He does
not say *so you must not*, because he is not that man and it is not his
clause to enforce; he says the arithmetic and stops, and lets her hold it.
When she asks whether he could not simply — he says *the clause is the
clause*, which is the only hard sentence he speaks in the book, and he
cannot look at her while he says it.

So the offer is a marriage that is not a marriage, and a life she may have
only in the two hours nobody is counting. It is meant, all of it. It is the
kindest offer she has ever had and it is the worst thing anyone says to her
in the book, and she comes back down to the flats unable to explain to Yannu
why she is worse.

**ch 18 — 39% — Yannu — the Shell Bank — 28 Longsun**
*Plot: — · Romance: —* (quiet chapter, sensory, and it carries the act)

He takes her to the hut because there is nowhere else and the tide is wrong.
Veth's boots on the nail; she does not ask and he does not say. He talks
about Kethren, the lime, the terraces, the Concession, the export of hands.
She tells him the four hours at twenty-two — the foundering nobody knows
about, the thirst that stopped and came back. He does not tell her about the
boots. Two secrets on the table, one of them still face-down. He also says,
without meaning anything by it, the sentence that will be the whole book:
*"It isn't gone. I have it. I can tell you exactly where."*

**ch 19 — 41% — Sahra — the north lobe — 6 Dust**
*Plot: Fun and Games · Romance: **MAYBE THIS COULD WORK***

Two hopes in one hour. First: the north lobe is not silting — the crust has
*lifted* a foot in six years, and the ground where Yannu has been quietly
steering set-downs is holding, and they work out why (living weed at the
margin). Maybe the Whiting can be managed. Second: if the survey is credited
at hazard rate rather than impressment rate, Sahra's balance clears at
thirty-eight instead of sixty-two, and thirty-eight is a number a person can
imagine. Two futures open in the same tide and they are both real for about
nine hours.

**ch 20 — 43% — Yannu — the Stone Ait — 15 Dust**
*Plot: Fun and Games · Romance: —*

**Under-reckoner Merrow Quen** audits the survey. The hazard rate is refused;
Sahra goes back to thirty-four years at a stroke. On the House's own rule,
read aloud in the audit and unremarked: *a working performed on the House's
account, witnessed by a reckoner, is credited against the worker's entry at
the assessed rate.* (Planted at 43%, used at 96%.) Merrow also, quietly and
without enthusiasm, tells Yannu that his six years of warrants are being
pulled and compared. In the same session Sahra's off-book fen work is nearly
found and is covered by an under-reckoner's clerical laziness rather than by
anyone's mercy.

**ch 21 — 46% — Sahra — the Stone Ait — 22 Dust**
*Plot: Fun and Games · Romance: —*

Yeshin comes down to be pre-assessed. Sahra watches the clerk write *capacity
presumed* in a fourteen-year-old's hand and stand her against a marked post
like a horse. Yeshin, bored and pleased with herself, asks what a composition
is. Sahra lies to her — cleanly, fluently, the way you lie to a child about a
diagnosis — and hears her own voice doing it.

**ch 22 — 48% — Yannu — Kell Ammar salt-house — 2 Ebb**
*Plot: Fun and Games · Romance: —* (quiet chapter)

Two days of storm; the survey stops; eleven people in one room with one lamp,
all pretending to sleep. Yannu and Sahra talk across four yards of floor at
the volume of breathing, all night, twice. He says the thing he has noticed:
*you don't touch anyone.* She says: *neither do you.* He says: *I can't.* She
does not answer, and the not-answering is the first admission either of them
has made. Two days the House is not paying for — the only two in the book.

**ch 23 — 50% — Sahra — the Wallow — 11 Ebb**
*Plot: **MIDPOINT** · Romance: **MIDPOINT OF LOVE*** — one sequence

The survey's finding lands, and Sahra takes it to its end out loud in front
of him: the Whiting is not silting. It is **full**. Which means every carry
in the Long Book is a promise drawn against a bank with nothing in it, and
her 1,806 outstanding are a fiction, and she has spent eleven years being a
unit of a currency that is about to be worth nothing. A false victory: she is
free, arithmetically, for about an hour — before she works out the rest of
it, which is that a currency nobody believes in is enforced harder, not
softer, and that the House will bury this and collect faster.

And in the same hour, both of them say the true thing. She tells him she was
**relieved** when she signed at nineteen — that she used the worst thing that
ever happened to her family as a place to put herself, so that nobody would
ever have to choose her. He tells her what grey actually is: that he has kept
a fraction of every load he has ever passed, eleven hundred of them over
fourteen years, permanently, in his hands, and that no book anywhere records
a span of it, and that he does not think it makes him nothing.

First deliberate touch: she puts her hand flat against his palm where the
feeling still reaches, and holds it there, and counts the seconds out loud so
that he knows how long it has been. Sixteen. She uses the word *want* for the
first time in the book.

---

## ACT II-B (ch 24–31, 52–67%) — Bad Guys Close In

**ch 24 — 52% — Yannu — the Stone Ait — 20 Ebb**
*Plot: Bad Guys Close In · Romance: —*

They bring the finding to Bel Osse. She reads it, believes it inside four
minutes, and **seals it**. Her reasons are laid out at length and they are
good: the carry is the Shelf's unit of account; every obligation is secured
against the Whiting; a public failure takes the water contracts, the granary
financing and the fever wards inside one season; she wrote the Hungry Year's
mortality return in her own hand at twenty-six and can quote the number. She
orders the pair kept on under seal and quietly reopens the Sur Ellun file.
She is not a villain and she does not move.

**ch 25 — 54% — Sahra — Ferrey — 29 Ebb**
*Plot: Bad Guys Close In · Romance: **INKLING OF DOUBT***

Sealed, the finding is a crime to speak — which removes the one lever Sahra
had. She had intended to take it to Dovra and renegotiate; now she cannot.
And Dovra, hearing only that the survey has been extended and that her
security's drawer is working at a third rate, moves the witnessing forward
again: high summer, 1219. First doubt, and it is not about him: it is that
the barrier has not moved a finger's width in half a book, and she begins
pre-emptively withdrawing from the only good thing in her year, on the
grounds that it is cheaper to stop now.

**ch 26 — 57% — Yannu — the Stone Ait — 7 Whitening**
*Plot: Bad Guys Close In · Romance: —*

The warrant audit lands. Merrow Quen has found the falsifications — six years
of them, two years serious. Bel Osse does not prosecute; she uses it. Sign
what I put in front of you or be struck from the roll and assessed, which
retires him and ends the map. He signs a warrant **reopening the north lobe**,
knowing that ground is finished. People will set down into it within a month.
He cannot tell Sahra, because the seal is also on him.

**ch 27 — 59% — Sahra — the north lobe — 14 Whitening**
*Plot: Bad Guys Close In · Romance: —*

House orders send Sahra to set down at the reopened north lobe, and the load
**comes back** inside the hour — surfaces through the crust while they are
still on the flats. She retakes it to keep it out of the reach and goes to
fifteen doing it. Yannu has to tell her he signed the warrant. It is the
first thing between them she cannot count her way out of, and she does not
forgive him in the chapter, and the book does not make her.

**ch 28 — 61% — Yannu — the factors' hall — 21 Whitening**
*Plot: Bad Guys Close In · Romance: **DEEPENING DOUBT***

Yannu goes to a salt-factor and asks the price of a bond-setter's indenture:
twenty years of his hands, worked at the buyer's speed. **280 carries against
2,140.** He does the arithmetic at the desk and the arithmetic is the answer.
He does not tell her. He tells Turi, who says: *"You didn't keep your hands,
boy. You kept your excuse."* He starts pulling away, and the pulling away is
not sulking; it is a man closing an account.

**ch 29 — 63% — Sahra — Sarrow-under-Wall — 3 Rime**
*Plot: Bad Guys Close In · Romance: —*

Sahra maps the returns against the House's own set-down registers and finds
the pattern: the Whiting is giving back **oldest first**, which means the fen
villages — set into for two centuries — are first in the queue, and
Sarrow-under-Wall is the oldest ground on the Shelf. She tries to warn Ansa;
Ansa cannot move 300 people on a sealed finding she is not allowed to have
been told. And Ansa says the thing: *"If you break it, they lose the fen and
the fen loses you. I love you and I need you married. Both are true."*

**ch 30 — 65% — Yannu — the Wallow — 15 Rime**
*Plot: Bad Guys Close In · Romance: —*

A bank gives at the Wallow's edge; four of the fen crew go under salt-slurry.
Sahra draws to **sixteen** to hold it off them — two past everything she has
ever had — and the thirst starts to go thin, and Yannu has to choose between
the rule he has kept for nine years and the woman in front of him. He takes
four carries in one pass. It **jumps**. He loses taste entirely and finds out
that evening with a mouthful of salt that is only texture. He does not regret
it. Sahra seats two carries and will be thirsty at a new baseline for the
rest of her life.

**ch 31 — 67% — Sahra — Sarrow-under-Wall — 28 Rime**
*Plot: **ALL IS LOST** · Romance: **RETREATING / SHIELDS UP***

The Wallow's live edge lets a lobe go on the spring tide. The returned comes
up through Sarrow-under-Wall: the well, the ground under the houses, the
children first. Nine dead in a day and more coming; the village is condemned
by evening; Ansa's hands. Turi, there because he is always there, takes three
carries off a child in one pass and **jumps** and loses the sight in his left
eye. And the fen's common ground — the security behind the composition —
loses its value in an afternoon.

Sahra, salt-thirsted, shaking, whitened to the hairline, will not let Yannu
near her. Not out of blame. Because she has just watched what happens to
people who depend on her, and she has one more thing left to pledge and it is
her whole life, and she is not going to be talked out of it by being touched.

---

## THE BREAK AND THE DARK (ch 32–35, 70–76%)

**ch 32 — 70% — Yannu — Kell Ammar — 2 Deepwinter**
*Plot: Bad Guys Close In (the barrier accelerates) · Romance: —*

**Dovra invokes the acceleration clause.** A material change in the value of
the pledged security entitles the creditor to demand execution within thirty
days: the Third Order, second schedule, printed on the face of the
instrument since 1063 and read aloud in ch 3 without anyone remarking on it.
Witnessing set for the new moon. Yannu learns it from a bill posted at the
salt-house, in the ordinary way, like weather. He reads it twice and goes to
find her.

**ch 33 — 72% — Sahra — the Shell Bank — 4 Deepwinter**
*Plot: — · Romance: **THE BREAK UP / BLACK MOMENT***

She has come to tell him before he can ask. She is going to the witnessing.

He offers the indenture: twenty years of his hands. She says the number
before he can — 280 against 2,140 — because she looked it up two months ago,
in Ebb, before she had any right to.

Then he says the thing Halim said, without knowing Halim said it: *marry him
and stay.* And she gives him the clause, flat, the way she gives every
number — issue is pledged from birth, a child of hers entered outside the
merger voids it for cause, thirty days, the fen, Yeshin at the pump — and
the cruelty is that it is not an excuse and he can check it. He does check
it. That is the worst part of the chapter. He says: *then what am I for.*
She says:
*nothing — and that is the point, and I have never been for anything either,
and I would rather one of us found that out somewhere other than the bottom
of a ledger.*

She leaves Halim's gloves — the ones he gave to Yannu, the ones Yannu gave to
her in Rime — on the nail beside Veth's boots.

Nothing is misunderstood in this chapter. Every fact on the table is true and
known to both of them. The break is the instrument closing, on schedule,
because the village died and made it worth less.

**ch 34 — 74% — Yannu — the Shell Bank — 9 Deepwinter**
*Plot: **DARK NIGHT OF THE SOUL** (Yannu) · Romance: —*

Alone, with the crust ticking. Turi comes out, half blind, and Yannu tells
him the truth about Veth: he did not find the boots. Veth asked and Yannu
walked him out and walked back alone. Turi does not absolve him. What Turi
says is that Yannu has spent nine years keeping his hands in reserve for a
life he had already decided not to have — *"You didn't keep your hands, boy.
You kept your excuse."* Yannu confronts it: Veth's hands were spent by a
factor for money, and his own have been spent by nobody for nothing, and only
one of those was a choice, and he has been treating the choice as a virtue.

**ch 35 — 76% — Sahra — Sarrow-under-Wall — 12 Deepwinter**
*Plot: **DARK NIGHT OF THE SOUL** (Sahra) · Romance: —*

Burying. No drawer will go onto returned ground, so **Sefa Quenn** is washing
the dead by hand, in buckets, the way it was done before 1010. Sahra — the
best drawer on the Shelf, eleven years and 334 carries into paying for this
village — stands and holds a bucket, and cannot construct any arithmetic in
which her carries have been worth more to Sarrow-under-Wall today than that
woman's hands.

And Sefa, wringing out a cloth, says the sentence: *"It doesn't wash out of
skin. It goes into you and stops. That's the only place it ever stops."*

Sahra hears it as grief. She writes it down anyway, because she writes
everything down.

---

## ACT III (ch 36–46, 78–100%)

**ch 36 — 78% — Yannu — the Shell Bank — 15 Deepwinter**
*Plot: **BREAK INTO THREE** · Romance: —*

She sends the sentence up with a fen boy, on a scrap, with no message
attached — the first thing either has said to the other since the break, and
it is somebody else's line.

Yannu puts it against fourteen years of his own body and it turns over.
**Grey is not damage. Grey is the load, finished.** A setter does not conduct;
he *keeps* a fraction, permanently, and what he keeps stops being a load and
becomes his numbness. The Whiting stores and has now run out of room; a
setter *ends* — and every full-grey pensioner on the Shelf is two hundred
years of proof that nobody has read, because the House classified it as an
occupational injury and paid a third rate for it.

Both plots reframe in one paragraph. There is a sink that does not fill and
it is people. And a working of that size, performed on the House's account
and witnessed, would be credited against an entry at the assessed rate — a
rule read aloud in an audit in Dust and unremarked by everyone in the room.

He walks to Kell Ammar in the dark. Nine hours.

**ch 37 — 80% — Sahra — Kell Ammar — 16 Deepwinter**
*Plot: **Finale: Gather the Team / Make the Plan** · Romance: —*

Sahra, Yannu, Sefa, Ansa, Turi (half blind), Merrow Quen, four fen setters,
and a room that does not believe them. The plan: a **demonstration**. Draw
four carries out of the Whiting's own crust and set them into a setter rather
than into ground; measure the ground before and over two tides after; measure
the setter's grey. If it holds, the Shelf has a sink that does not fill, and
the House can be made to fund it — which means carries earned against the
Book at a rate nobody has ever tested.

Turi volunteers, over Yannu's objection, and wins the argument by pointing
out that he is already full grey and has nothing left to spend but the thing
Yannu is trying to protect him from spending.

Sahra has eleven days to the witnessing and says so, once, and then does not
mention it again.

**ch 38 — 83% — Yannu — the Stone Ait — 18 Deepwinter**
*Plot: **Finale: Make the Plan** · Romance: —*

Getting Bel Osse to witness. The leverage is her own fear: if the House will
not send a reckoner, the demonstration happens in front of the fen and the
factors anyway, and the thing she has spent a season containing arrives as
rumour instead of as policy. She agrees to witness. She does not agree to
believe. In the same hour, in a different building, Dovra refuses to move the
witnessing by a single day and cites the clause: nine days.

**ch 39 — 85% — Sahra — the Nine Marks — 21 Deepwinter**
*Plot: **Finale: Execute the Plan** · Romance: —*

The demonstration. Four carries drawn out of the crust — the first time in
twelve hundred years anyone has drawn *from* the Whiting rather than into it
— and set into Turi Osse instead of into ground. It works. The ground reads
clean at the first tide and clean again at the second. Turi's grey advances
from the hands into the chest; by evening he cannot feel himself breathing
and describes it, accurately and obscenely, to his niece.

Bel Osse writes it down, because the rule makes her write down what she
witnesses, and the entry goes into the field ledger with her initials on it.

**ch 40 — 87% — Yannu — the Wallow — 23 Deepwinter**
*Plot: **Finale: HIGH TOWER SURPRISE** · Romance: —*

Two things on the same tide.

Turi dies. Cold, on the flats, unfelt — a man who could not feel himself
breathing and therefore could not feel himself stopping.

And the Wallow's whole live edge lets go, three days before the spring
tide anyone budgeted for: twenty-two miles of weeping crust, coming down the
Third Reach into the Sarrow, the Nissa, and Amrith's cisterns inside eleven
hours.

The plan they have just proved needs decades, a funded instrument, and a
relay of hundreds. **There are no relays.** A load moves thing → drawer →
setter → end, and nothing else takes it, and the rule that makes a setter the
only sink in the world is the same rule that means only *one* setter can be
in the chain. What they have is eleven hours, one drawer, and one setter, and
the price of what is coming has just been quoted at a rate nobody budgeted
for.

**ch 41 — 89% — Sahra — the Wallow — 23 Deepwinter, evening**
*Plot: **Finale: DIG DEEP DOWN** · Romance: **GRAND GESTURE*** — one decision

Sahra works it in front of everyone, out loud, in the clerk's cadence she has
used since she was nine. The live edge is about two thousand carries. She
holds fourteen. A live pass means nothing seats **as long as neither of them
breaks**, which means she can take it and keep taking it — and it means she
will founder past any return, and carry salt for the rest of her life, and
never draw again.

She will destroy the exact faculty her debt is denominated in. It is the only
way to pay it and it makes her permanently unable to pay anything, ever
again, and she says that part out loud too because she has never in her life
left a figure out of a total.

And she chooses him, on the page, in front of Ansa and Merrow and the crew:
not any setter — him, because no one else could hold her rhythm for ten
hours, and because she is not going to have this be a thing she did alone.
She asks. She tells him to say no now if he is going to.

**ch 42 — 91% — Yannu — the Shell Bank / the Wallow — 23–24 Deepwinter, night**
*Plot: **Finale: Execute the New Plan** · Romance: —*

His answer, and the walk out at moonset. He tells her in plain words what
full grey is: no touch, no smell, and taste already gone, and he will not be
able to feel her hand afterwards, ever, and asks whether she wants that. She
says yes and says why. They set their terms like two professionals, because
that is what they are: she will say the numbers aloud, continuously, so that
he knows what is happening inside his own hands when he can no longer tell.

The clause is in the room and neither of them pretends otherwise. Tomorrow it
is still live; the night is the two hours nobody is counting, and they take
it on those terms and name them. This is not defiance and they do not call it
that — it is a decision made inside an instrument that has not been
discharged yet, by two people who can both read one.

The second and last open-door scene, brief, and entirely about the border of
what he can still feel and where it will be tomorrow.

Bel Osse and two under-reckoners take up position on the bank at the fourth
hour, because a working on the House's account must be witnessed by a
reckoner to be credited, and Bel Osse — who does not believe, and who wants
the record either way — has come herself.

**ch 43 — 93% — Sahra — the Wallow — 24 Deepwinter, low water**
*Plot: **Finale: Execute the New Plan** · Romance: —*

The lowest tide of the year. Sahra draws.

Nine. Fourteen. Twenty. She goes past the record in the Long Book in the
second hour and past anything anyone has words for by the fourth. She names
every carry aloud as she takes it, the way she named two bays of rot to an
empty granary floor on 9 Thaw. Somewhere in the fifth hour **the thirst
stops**, and she keeps going, and only the reader and Yannu know what that
means.

**ch 44 — 96% — Yannu — the Wallow — 24 Deepwinter**
*Plot: **Finale: Execute the New Plan — the single action** · Romance: **HEA
begins on the page***

Ten hours. Yannu takes all of it, into himself, and not into ground.

The grey goes past the wrist, past the elbow, into the shoulder, the mouth,
the nose, the skin of his back. Around the eighth hour he stops being able to
feel her hands at all and keeps going on her voice, and she does not stop
counting for two hours, and the last hundred carries are passed by a man who
has no evidence he is still holding anything except a woman saying numbers.

The reach comes up clean. The tide comes in over clean ground for the first
time in six years, and the Sarrow and the Nissa and eighty thousand people's
water are still there in the morning.

And Bel Osse, on the bank, does the thing the rule makes her do: assesses the
working and enters it. **2,306 carries, to the account of Ottun.** Against
2,140 outstanding. The composition is discharged in the House's field ledger,
on the flats, with the water coming up over the legs of the entry desk and
Merrow Quen holding the lamp.

One action. It ends the Whiting's failure by proving where a load can be
finished, and it discharges the composition by crediting more carries than
the debt, in the same hour, on the same page, witnessed by the same officer.

**ch 45 — 98% — Yannu — Kell Ammar — 26 Deepwinter**
*Plot: Final Image (resolution) · Romance: **HEA / HFN***

Aftermath, and the choosing, on the page, with both of them in the room.

Dovra reads the discharge, checks the arithmetic twice, says *"then it is
discharged,"* and goes. She does not soften and she is not ruined; Nesuir is
solvent and she will be at the next quarter's reckoning. Halim, released,
gives Sahra the tally-ring to break herself and says the first selfish
sentence of his life — and before he does, he finishes the sentence he could
not finish in ch 17, which now costs him nothing and is worth nothing and he
says it anyway. The clause died with the entry. Yeshin will be assessed at
sixteen against a clean line
and complains about the queue. Bel Osse is already drafting the instrument
that will make setter-service compulsory, and tells them so to their faces,
because she wants it on the record that she was not converted.

Sahra cannot stop drinking and it does not help and it never will. Yannu
cannot feel the cup she puts into his hand. He says so — *"I cannot feel your
hand. Tell me it is there and I will believe you. That is going to be the
arrangement now."* — and she tells him, and goes on telling him, and they
choose each other out loud in a room with eleven other people in it, both
alive, both present, nothing hidden and nothing undone.

**ch 46 — 100% — Sahra — Third Reach, low water — 27 Deepwinter**
*Plot: **FINAL IMAGE** · Romance: HEA*

Dawn on the Third Reach, the same hour and the same mud as ch 1, the
tide-bell at Kell Ammar counting. Sahra names nothing aloud, because there is
nothing to name and never will be again. Her cup is full and she empties it
and fills it again and it does nothing.

Behind them, out on the white, the House's new account has put forty setters
on the marks, and there will be four hundred by Thaw, and it will take
seventy years, and Bel Osse's levy is coming. The work has barely started and
it is going to be somebody's whole century.

Sahra puts her hand into Yannu's and tells him that she has done it, because
he cannot tell.

Nothing in the final quarter arrives unpaid for.

| F2 | **Grey is keeping, not loss** | ch 2 (Turi: *"It isn't gone, boy. It's in me."*) | ch 18 (Yannu: *"I have it. I can tell you exactly where."*); ch 23 (eleven hundred loads, kept, unrecorded) | ch 36 — Break Into Three: a setter is the only place a load ends | Dialogue |
| F3 | **Sefa's sentence** | ch 12 (Sefa keeps the pre-Draw arithmetic) | ch 29 (the returns follow the oldest set-downs) | ch 35 → ch 36 — *"It goes into you and stops. That's the only place it ever stops."* | Dialogue |
| F4 | **The jump (>3 carries in one pass)** | ch 8 (Yannu loses the smell of smoke) | ch 30 (loses taste for Sahra); ch 31 (Turi loses an eye) | ch 44 — full grey, ~2,000 carries in one continuous pass | Action |

| F9 | **Standing water on the Wallow** | ch 1 (closing image; Sahra does not know what she is looking at) | ch 2 (129 paces lost); ch 14 (the first return); ch 19 (the crust has lifted a foot) | ch 23 — the Whiting is full; ch 31 — the lobe gives | Symbolic / action |

| F15 | **Yeshin's capacity** | ch 1 (the apple) | ch 3 (*capacity presumed*); ch 21 (pre-assessed, asks what a composition is) | ch 45 — assessed at sixteen against a clean line | Action |
| F16 | **Sur Ellun failed in 1148** | ch 2 (walkers' lore: no set into moving water) | ch 24 (Bel Osse reopens the file) | ch 40 — the file is still closed; there is no second sink and no rescue from the sea | Direct |
| F17 | **Sahra names loads aloud** | ch 1 | ch 6 (Yannu notices); ch 13; ch 21 | ch 43–44 — she counts for ten hours and it is the only thing keeping him working | Action |
| F18 | **Living weed at the margin holds** | ch 19 | ch 29 (the returns avoid the weeded margins) | ch 39 — the demonstration is sited on weeded ground so the measurement is clean | Action |
| F19 | **Turi is Bel Osse's uncle** | ch 2 (mentioned once, in passing, by a third party) | ch 24 (she does not ask after him); ch 37 (he volunteers partly to make her watch) | ch 39–40 — she witnesses his demonstration and his death and does not change | Naming |
| F20 | **The bond-setter's indenture** | ch 4 (what the factors buy) | ch 8 (Veth was one); ch 28 (280 against 2,140) | ch 33 — offered and refused; it is the only door and it is too small | Direct |
| F21 | **The lowest tides fall in Deepwinter** | ch 2 (walkers' calendar) | ch 22 (the storm; the crew count months); ch 37 (eleven days) | ch 43 — the working is only possible on 24 Deepwinter | Direct |

**Deliberate unpaid thread, and why:** Bel Osse's compulsory setter-service is
raised in ch 45 and not resolved. It is not a dangling plant; it is the book
saying out loud that the instrument the leads invented will be used on people,
and it is stated as a threat rather than a hook.

# PART 3 — QUESTIONS THE BOOK RAISES

| Question | Raised | Answered |
|---|---|---|
| What is wrong with the Whiting? | ch 1 (standing water) | ch 23 — it is full; ground carries and has a capacity |
| Why did the north lobe close? | ch 5 | ch 14 / ch 26 — Yannu falsified the warrant |
| What is the Ottun debt and can it be paid? | ch 3 | ch 10 — 2,140 carries or a house that assumes them; ch 44 — 2,306 carries, once |
| Can anyone release Sahra? | ch 5 | ch 10 (Dovra: no), ch 17 (Halim: no), ch 28 (Yannu: not enough) |
| Then can she simply marry him and live as she likes? | ch 17 (Halim offers half of it) | ch 17 — no; the alienation clause makes issue outside the merger a default, and neither Halim nor Dovra can waive what is pledged forward. Restated by Sahra in ch 33 and dead at ch 44 |
| What happened to Ines Ottun? | ch 1 (referenced) | ch 9 / ch 18 — foundered at the eleventh carry; died over three years |
| What happened to Veth? | ch 2 (the boots) | ch 34 — Yannu walked him out |
| Where does a load actually go? | ch 2 (theme stated) | ch 36 — nowhere, except into a setter, where it ends |
| Is there a second sink? | ch 24 (Sur Ellun reopened) | ch 40 — no. There are only people |
| What does Sahra actually want? | ch 3 (the entry struck) | ch 23 (him, and she says the word) |
| Will Yeshin be free? | ch 3 (*capacity presumed*) | ch 45 — assessed against a clean line |
| What does the ending cost? | ch 8 (the jump), ch 9 (foundering) | ch 44 — her capacity, permanently; his touch, smell, and what taste was left |

# PART 4 — STRUCTURAL CHECKS

- **Chapters:** 46. **Words:** 120,000 at ~2,600. **Act I:** ch 1–11 (0–24%).
  **Act II:** ch 12–35 (26–76%). **Act III:** ch 36–46 (78–100%).
- **POV:** Sahra odd / Yannu even through ch 43, then Yannu 44, Yannu 45,
  Sahra 46. Longest absence for either lead: two consecutive chapters.
- **Catalyst and Adhesion:** ch 5, one event. **Midpoint and Midpoint of
  Love:** ch 23, one sequence. **Dig Deep Down and Grand Gesture:** ch 41, one
  decision.
- **Dark Night:** both leads, separately, on the page — ch 34 (Yannu), ch 35
  (Sahra).
- **Black Moment (ch 33) is caused by All Is Lost (ch 31):** the village dies,
  the security craters, the acceleration clause fires in ch 32, and the
  witnessing is set for the new moon. Remove ch 31 and there is no ch 33.
- **Try-fail through the middle:** ch 13 yes-but; ch 14 no-and; ch 17
  no-and; ch 19 yes-but; ch 20 no-and; ch 24 no-and; ch 25 no-and; ch 26
  no-and; ch 27 no-and; ch 29 no-but; ch 30 yes-but; ch 31 no-and. Eleven of
  twelve are yes-but or no-and.
- **MICE:** opened I (what is wrong with the Whiting, ch 1) → C (Sahra's lie,
  ch 3) → E (the weep, ch 5). Closed E (ch 44, the reach comes up clean) → C
  (ch 45, she chooses out loud) → I (ch 46, the answer is seventy years of
  people walking the marks).
- **Nothing in the final quarter is new:** live pass ch 15, foundering ch 9,
  the jump ch 8, grey-as-keeping ch 2, the credit rule ch 3 and ch 20, no
  relays ch 5 and ch 20, the Deepwinter tides ch 2.
